**Job Summary And Qualifications**
"We had a patient who had just lost her husband and arrived in a completely catatonic state – she wasn't eating, drinking, walking, or engaging at all. With the care of our nursing team in talking to her, group therapy, and coordinated care with her physician - including medication management - we helped guide her through the depths of her trauma and get re-acclimated to life. Before she was discharged, she told us, 'I'm a little happier. I'm still grieving, but now I know how to cope with it.' In that moment, I knew I was in the right place."
  
  
Ann, Behavioral Health RN at HCA Healthcare
  
  
As a Behavioral Health nurse, you’ll be at the forefront of improving mental health care, helping patients find stability and hope within the community you serve. As a Resident I Mental Health Nurse, you’ll care for patients with a range of mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and co-occurring medical issues—including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety. You’ll build skills in de-escalation, trauma-informed care, therapeutic communication, and safe psychotropic medication administration, while working closely with psychiatrists, providers, therapists, social workers, and more. Because all nursing involves mental health, you’ll be well-prepared to grow within Behavioral Health or transition into other specialties as your career evolves.
  
  

* Patient Care Delivery: As a Resident I Graduate Nurse, you will implement nursing care plans under the supervision of an experienced Registered Nurse in a high-quality, empathetic, and patient-centered manner
* Documentation: Document observations, interactions and patient responses and report to your assigned RN, RN Preceptor, Clinical Nurse Coordinator or Charge Nurse
* Patient Education: You educate patients on their treatment plans, diagnoses, medications, possible side effects, follow-up measures and more
* Clinical Excellence: You will engage in evidence-based best practices that enhance the patient experience and patient outcomes, including SAFETY rounding, communication fundamentals/AIDET, Teach-Back, Narrating Care, etc

What qualifications you will need:
  
  

* Authorization to Test - NCLEX-RN
* Basic Cardiac Life Support must be obtained within 7 days of employment start date
* Nonviolent Crisis Intervention must be obtained within 30 days of employment start date
* NCLEX Examination Appointment Confirmation
* (RN) Registered Nurse must be obtained within 90 days of employment start date
* Associate Degree, or Bachelors Degree

No Travel Required
